No existing file was edited.

Key methodological finding for the whole workflow: on this Muse-in-headset montage blinks are NOT on AF7/AF8. Every channel is referenced to Fpz over the nasion, so a blink is one identical negative pulse on TP9, TP10 and the AUX/Oz cup (run 2 medians 39.4/40.0/39.6 uV, half width ~100 ms, irregular intervals) and only a 3-16 uV gradient on the forehead pair. The frontal detector as specified and the repo's blinkmask (100 uV) sit at the noise floor; the 'blinks' numbers in state_of_flash.json (0.0-0.3/min) are that undercount. Any sibling marker using TP9/TP10/AUX for spectral work should treat these pulses (6-15 per min, 50-60 uV, 0.5-8 Hz) as blink artifact on the ear and Oz channels.

Does the data match 'eyes irritated, not drowsy'? Partly. For irritation: blinking on task was suppressed to 1/5-1/3 of the resting rate in every session (the dry-eye mechanism), blinks were held while a 12 Hz cell flickered and released the instant it went black, and run 2 blinked about twice as often as run 1 at matched minutes (+6.0/min [+4.3, +7.9], permutation p < 1e-4) from its first minute on. Against it: no rise within either run (run 2 slightly fell), no long blinks, no bursting trend. For not-drowsy: no long or slow blinks anywhere, durations flat. The forehead ache cannot be tested by this family; the only forehead signal is a ten-fold rise of 0.1-0.5 Hz drift on AF7/AF8 through run 2 (contact/sweat/pressure under the headset), absent in run 1 and the reference day.

Which run was better, from the eyes' side: run 1. It blinked at near the reference-day level (6.8 vs 4.1/min), followed the new cell with a saccade 0.60 times per change (run 2: 0.23), its wandering eye movements and forehead drift settled over the run; run 2 blinked twice as much from the start, wandered five times more by its end and its forehead contact drifted ten-fold. Run 1's only blemish is a noisy first 5 min (26.6 horizontal events per min and high slow drift during the full-field white calibration and sweep, i.e. settling).

Unmeasurable/weak: pre-task baselines (87-92 % movement), post-task windows (0.1-0.4 min), absolute blink duration (band-passed reference pulse, not a vertical EOG), any direct forehead-ache marker.

What this means for the symptom claims: (a) the forehead electrodes were cleaner in run 2 than run 1 (run 1 = reference-day level) and settle during every run, so a frontal high-frequency or broadband marker that is lower in run 2 or declines through a run is contact, not relief; a frontal marker that rises against the contact trend (AF7 20-100 Hz in run 1 only) is the one thing contact does not explain; (b) no pre-flicker baseline exists in any session, so the order confound (2 h later, prior exposure) cannot be removed; (c) the 12 Hz and 9 Hz stimuli do not reach AF7/AF8 measurably, so frontal lit-vs-dark effects are not photic driving - but a ~30% lower frontal 1-4 Hz power during lit cells is a behavioural (fixation) difference every frontal slow-wave/EOG marker inherits, and it exists on the symptom-free day too; (d) head movement was too rare to matter, but TP10 was loose from minute 10 of run 2, which contaminates every ear-based marker there and produces a fake 'jaw EMG rise'; (e) jaw/temporalis EMG cannot be shown to drive the forehead signal tonight (no positive ear-forehead coupling, unlike the reference day) but the ears are not a clean EMG reference; (f) the helper sof.timeline puts 1.6 min of colour flicker per run into the DARK pool and half the blue plane's black cells into TAGGED, and the 100 uV blink detector finds ~0 blinks on task, so blink-rate markers from it are unmeasurable. On the user's 'which run was better' from a contact standpoint only: run 2 had the better forehead contact (60 Hz 0.45/0.63 vs 1.70/1.98 uV) and clean AF7/AF8 throughout, but a loose TP10 for the last 20 min; run 1 had clean ears and reference-day-level forehead noise. Not reported as a finding because it is not a symptom marker. Timestamp caveat: eeg.csv times are packet-stamped (median dt 1e-4 s, 95th percentile 30 ms), so all spectral work indexes samples at the nominal 256 Hz and uses the time column only to align stage logs (within ~0.1 s); the overall rate is 255.98-255.99 Hz with no dropped data.
